extracted.intended_audience: writers applying to the Tin House Summer Workshop (poets, novelists, short fiction and creative nonfiction writers)
extracted.subtask_short: apply to Tin House Summer Workshop
extracted.subtask_description: Information and requirements for applying to and attending the Tin House Summer Workshop: program dates/location, genres offered, application materials and deadline, costs, available financial accommodations, program components, accessibility, and contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program dates and location
rubrics_metrics.description: The workshop will be held from July 12 to July 19 at Reed College in Portland, Oregon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates and site specify when and where the in-person program occurs; applicants should plan travel and availability accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres and class size
rubrics_metrics.description: Program features poetry, novel, short fiction, and creative nonfiction workshops with eight participants per class.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops are small (eight participants), indicating an intimate classroom setting and likely limited openings per genre; applicants should note genre-specific placement and competitive small cohorts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application writing sample
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants submitted a writing sample of up to four poems totaling no more than 10 pages or up to 4,000 words of prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear formatting/length limits apply: either up to four poems (≤10 pages total) or prose ≤4,000 words. Follow the specified form and length limits on the program website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application fee and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications required a $30 application fee and were due by February 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must be submitted by the stated deadline with the fee; note that fee waiver availability is mentioned elsewhere (see financial accommodations). See website for application form and complete guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tuition and housing costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Tuition is $2,000; the fee for room and board in the Reed College dormitories is $600.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should budget for both tuition and optional housing; these are the listed program costs and may be subject to change—check the program website for current rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial aid and fee waivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholarships, payment plans, and application fee waivers were available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program offers financial accommodations; applicants needing assistance should consult the website or contact program staff about scholarship criteria, payment-plan options, or application-fee waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program components and participant experience
rubrics_metrics.description: The program offers one-on-one meetings with faculty and agents, craft lectures, author conversations, generative exercises, readings, and social events (prom and karaoke nights).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond workshops, the schedule includes mentorship, craft instruction, public readings, generative practice, and community/social events—these shape the workshop experience and opportunities for networking and feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility accommodations
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessibility accommodations included elevator access; accessible doorways, pathways, bathrooms, dorm rooms, and dining hall; golf cart rides to and from all dorms and events; reserved accessible seating for all lectures, workshops, and public readings; and ASL interpretation at all readings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program provides multiple accessibility services; applicants with access needs are advised to contact the executive workshop director via e-mail for additional details or to arrange specific accommodations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact and further information
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact information: Tin House Summer Workshop, 2601 NW Thurman Street, Portland, OR 97210. (503) 345-5123. Lance Cleland, Executive Workshop Director. Website: https://tinhouse.com/workshop
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For questions, application forms, complete guidelines, or to request accommodations, use the provided phone, address, director contact, or official website.
